changes.change: 'Hell is a democracy. Heaven is a kingdom.' (attributed to John of Kronstadt) replaced by Bossuet: '…the royal throne is not the throne of a man, but the throne of God himself.' Source added; alias 'Divine right of kings' added.
changes.rationale: The slogan is the motto of the Moscow monarchist newspaper Zemshchina (issue 6, August 1990) and was first attributed to John of Kronstadt in 1998. Bossuet's Politique is the classic Catholic statement of divine-right monarchy, which matches the route (God as source of legitimacy; the temporal ruler does not direct the church).
sources: Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet, Politique tirée des propres paroles de l’Écriture sainte (1709), trans. in J. H. Robinson (ed.), Readings in European History, vol. 2 (Boston, 1906), pp. 273–277, via University of Washington course text
Petr Pashkov, '«Демократия в аду, а на Небе — Царство»: говорил ли так св. Иоанн?', Aletheia blog on VK (undated)
English Wikiquote, 'John of Kronstadt', lists a variant without source
unverified: Pashkov's archival claims (Zemshchina issue 6, August 1990; first attribution 1998) were not checked against the newspapers themselves
Book, article and proposition numbers of the Bossuet passage in the French original

changes.change: 'For our friends, everything. For our enemies, not even justice.' (attributed to Juan Perón) replaced by a sourced editorial description of welfare conditional on political loyalty, referring to the literature on the 'authoritarian welfare state'.
changes.rationale: Argentine sources report the saying only as attributed to Perón, with no primary source. Using it also presented Peronism as the defining case of 'social autocracy', which is an editorial judgment the classification should not make.
sources: Natalia Forrat, 'The Authoritarian Welfare State: A Marginalized Concept', CHSS Working Paper 12-005, Northwestern University, September 2012
La Nación, '“Al enemigo, ni justicia”: del dicho al hecho' (the saying 'is attributed to Perón')
changes.openQuestion: The name 'Social Autocracy / Social Authoritarianism' was not found as an established term; logged for R65.

changes.change: 'It's better to be hanged for loyalty than rewarded for betrayal' (attributed to Vladimir Putin) replaced by an editorial description quoting Henry Hale's definition of patronal politics.
changes.rationale: The quotation appears only on quotation websites, without a source. 'Patronalism' is Hale's term; his definition is the authoritative statement of the concept.
sources: Henry E. Hale, Patronal Politics: Eurasian Regime Dynamics in Comparative Perspective (Cambridge University Press, 2015), Introduction, pp. 9–10 (publisher's excerpt)

changes.change: The Gorter extract, which was cut off and ended with the fragment 'And the party.', replaced by the exact line from the same section: 'Factory organisation or union together with party! The unity of both!' Source added.
changes.rationale: The original passage is genuine (Gorter 1921, section 3) but was garbled and unsourced.
sources: Herman Gorter, The Organisation of the Proletariat’s Class Struggle (KAPD, 1921), section 3, trans. D. A. Smart (1977), Marxists Internet Archive

changes.change: A passage attributed to Pannekoek ('As the driving force of the conscious minority…') replaced by Pannekoek (1936): '…a party is an organization that aims to lead and control the working class.' Source added.
changes.rationale: The passage could not be traced to any Pannekoek text. The 1936 line states the reason his current rejected a distinct party alongside the councils, which is the route's distinction.
sources: Anton Pannekoek, 'The Party and Class' (1936), Marxists Internet Archive
unverified: Original publication venue of the 1936 text (the archive notes close variants titled 'Party and Working Class' and 'The Party and the Working Class')

changes.change: q_soe ('Should state-owned companies play a central role in the economy?', unchanged wording) moved from the strongman branch to the elected-government chain of economic-mechanism questions, after public credit (Social Credit) and before q_trad. In the strongman branch, q_authWelf 'No' now leads straight to q_klepto.
changes.rationale: State capitalism could only be reached by answering that one powerful leader should govern, although its card describes Singapore's Temasek model and the tradition is not defined by personal rule. R42 had already recorded this as an unresolved counterexample. Strongman supporters of state ownership still reach Autocratic capitalism.
sources: Existing card source: Lim Boon Heng, Temasek chairman, speech of 5 December 2013

changes.change: 'I care not a fig for his holiness’ excommunications…' (attributed to Henry VIII) replaced by the Act of Supremacy 1534: '…the only supreme head in earth of the Church of England…'. Source added.
changes.rationale: No source for the attributed sentence was found. The Act is the legal statement of a temporal ruler directing the church, which is the route's distinction.
sources: Act of Supremacy, 26 Hen. VIII c. 1 (1534), Parliamentary Archives HL/PO/PU/1/1534/26H8n1; text via University of Oregon course page; wording checked against two further transcriptions

changes.change: 'If you must break the law, do it to seize power. In all other cases, observe it.' (presented as Caesar's words) replaced by the lines of Euripides that Caesar is reported to have always quoted, in Rolfe's public-domain translation. Author now 'Julius Caesar, quoting Euripides'.
changes.rationale: The previous line is a loose modern rendering of Euripides presented as Caesar's own saying.
sources: Suetonius, Divus Julius 30, trans. J. C. Rolfe (Loeb, 1914), via Lexundria; Cicero, De Officiis 3.82 (cited by Suetonius)
unverified: That the previous wording is Robert Graves's translation (1957)

changes.change: 'How should the state be undermined? Withdrawal of cooperation / Insurrection' becomes 'Should the state be undermined mainly by withdrawing cooperation from it? Yes / No'. Routing is unchanged; two stale answer-icon keys removed.
changes.rationale: Anarcho-capitalists, Hoppeans, geoanarchists, left-Rothbardians and anarcho-distributists could only continue by choosing 'Insurrection', a strategy most of them do not hold.
